The upload staging copy (scratchpad/liveup, 577 files) is byte-identical to `git ls-tree b1b3684d apps/edge-bff`: no file differs and none is missing. edge-app.js, edge-client.js, edge-labels.js, edge-session.js and edge-boot.js served by app.edgefinance.id have the same sha256 as the commit. Railway: deployment c658d282 is SUCCESS with no repo source (M514); its start command uses `--no-proxy-headers`; 1 replica; the only domain is app.edgefinance.id (no *.up.railway.app domain).

Live variables, by name or reference only. EDGE_SESSION_SECRET, EDGE_CODE_SECRET, EDGE_MFA_KEY, EDGE_OWNER, EDGE_LOGIN, EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER and EDGE_ENVIRONMENT are `${{edge-bff.*}}` references. The worker and terminal keys reference their own services (M513 S3). Checked as true/false only: EDGE_ENVIRONMENT is not local, EDGE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN is https://app.edgefinance.id, EDGE_EMAIL_MODE is resend, and EDGE_EMAIL_FROM holds no-reply@mail.edgefinance.id. The start lines of both sites show the same shared_keys marks (72c3eb9b9fbd, f2434edf73f3, d9b2c2e78681). The live start line has loops=3: backtest, housekeeping and the email sender.

Probes, unauthenticated. GET /ready 200. GET /version answers {site: live, commit: null}. GET /api/v1/auth/config answers registration false, prelaunch true, guests true and hidden_tabs [admin, monitor]. POST sign-in with an unknown login (Origin set) gives 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS with no Set-Cookie, so in pre-launch no registration cookie is sent. The same POST without an Origin gives 403 ORIGIN_REJECTED. POST /api/v1/hooks/../auth/sign-in (path-as-is) gives 404. POST mfa/verify without a session gives 401. code/resend with purpose register gives 403 REGISTRATION_CLOSED. A forged 64-hex `__Host-edge_session` on /auth/session gives 401. /auth/guest gives the visitor answer (plan guest, terminal.view, BBCA). OPTIONS with a foreign Origin gives 405 with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. /qrcode-generator.js, /mfa, /forgot, /reset, /login, /register and /verify all give 200.

Who may sign in, from the code. main.py:840-878 checks every password (sign_in_try, then verify) before deciding SIGN_IN_CLOSED. needs_mfa reads the account's own catalog grants ('*' or admin.access). principal.py Auth.resolve applies the pre-launch rule on every request. Local suites pass against the throwaway Postgres: test_c3c_accounts, test_live_beta_sessions, test_m512_client_address, test_beta_live_site and test_auth_flows, 72 passed.

Admin's first sign-in on a live-site build (real routes, real browser; EDGE_SITE=live, pre-launch, guests). The sign-in leads to /mfa. The QR code and 10 recovery codes appear, and Continue is blocked until 'I have saved' is ticked. The code is accepted and the page lands on /terminal, not the Monitor (experiment test_probe_mfa_pages.py: 'landing after first enrolment: /terminal').

Sessions of the two sites. The beta accepts only sessions with user_id NULL (store.py:112). The live site joins the session to an account (accounts.py:181-186, `s.user_id = u.user_id`), so neither site resolves the other's session; the cookies are host-only `__Host-` cookies. ACCOUNT_SESSIONS (accounts.py:367) ends user #1's beta sessions on a live reset, change or sign-out-all (M513 S2). The beta's seed keeps the live admin's own password, because edge_account_login.py leaves seed_verifier_sha256 as it is (accounts.py seed).

CSRF and Origin. Every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE route in app/*.py that has a session uses the writer dependency (CSRF), and none uses the plain principal (grep). The only routes exempt from the Origin check are under /api/v1/hooks/, and the only route there is the signed Resend hook. A pending MFA session reaches only MFA_OPEN; the sign-in and the MFA verify each issue a new token.

Throttles with Railway's header. throttle.py forwarded_hop takes the entry one left of the right-most (EDGE_HOPS=1) over every header line. The M512 fix commit 13f40871 is an ancestor of b1b3684d, and uvicorn runs with --no-proxy-headers. My probe entered Railway's edge at ord1 (x-railway-edge: ord1) and the replica runs in sfo, so the 2-entry header M512 measured already crossed regions. Suspected, not verified: an entry edge in Asia (where the users are) gives the same 2 entries; M512's probe ran only from this machine.

Forgot password and its mail. The code lives 300 s (auth_flows.CODE_SECONDS) and email_texts.py says 5 minutes, used once; the subject carries the code, as CONTRACT 5 asks. A reset revokes every session of the account (beta ones included), clears the password and MFA failure counts, and sends 'password changed'. Public DNS for the sender is in place: DKIM at resend._domainkey.mail.edgefinance.id, SPF and MX at send.mail.edgefinance.id, DMARC p=none at edgefinance.id. Not verified: no `email_sent` line exists in the live log since the 09:52 start, so delivery through Resend has never run on the live site. The first real Forgot password will be its first test. I sent no reset and no email.

Pending admin sessions from the smoke. http_smoke.py kept its cookies in per-call memory jars (never written to disk), so the two pending admin sessions it made (they expire after 8 h idle) are held by nobody.

The repository was left clean (`git status` empty). The experiments live only in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-saniti/f3bec3b8-f6e3-5a54-b257-4a56b384bdc8/scratchpad/checker_after/exp/, with screenshots exp_landing.png, exp_after_recovery.png and exp_recovery_locked.png in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-saniti/f3bec3b8-f6e3-5a54-b257-4a56b384bdc8/scratchpad/checker_after/.

findings.title: A new or lost phone: after the fresh code the /mfa page leaves for the workspace and never shows the new authenticator's set-up, so CONTRACT 4's way to replace an authenticator does not work
findings.evidence: Verified locally, not on the running site: it would need the admin's sign-in. The build was the deployed commit (liveup equals b1b3684d, and the served static files hash-equal) with the live settings (site live, pre-launch, guests), real routes and Chromium; the experiment is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-saniti/f3bec3b8-f6e3-5a54-b257-4a56b384bdc8/scratchpad/checker_after/exp/test_probe_mfa_pages.py and test_probe_mfa_pages2.py. Steps: the admin is enrolled, signs out, signs in and presses 'Set up an authenticator app'. The server refuses with the 10-minute sentence (as designed). The admin then enters a recovery code: output 'after the recovery code: path /mfa QR shown 0 auth-codes shown 0' and 'a new authenticator waits on the server: True' (mfa_totp.pending_nonce set). With the old phone's code instead: 'old phone code: path /mfa QR shown 0 waiting on server True'. Opening /mfa while signed in shows no set-up button ('set-up button 0'). The screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-saniti/f3bec3b8-f6e3-5a54-b257-4a56b384bdc8/scratchpad/checker_after/exp_after_recovery.png shows the Terminal with /mfa in the address bar. Mechanism: Edge.mfaVerify (static/edge-client.js:252-253) adopts the fresh session and adopt dispatches edge-auth (:234). App.authMode then returns null once authenticated with access.next null (static/edge-app.js:2708), so the workspace replaces MfaForm. MfaForm's `if (resumeEnrol && !enrol) ... await startEnrol()` (:861) still calls enroll, but its QR and the new recovery codes render into a view that is no longer shown. CONTRACT.md:266 says the /mfa page 'then starts the set-up again by itself'. The browser test meant to hold this (tests/test_decisions_small.py:204-222) stubs verify with {'ok': True}, an answer with no csrf_token, so auth stays null and the App never switches; it cannot catch this. Consequence for a lost phone: each live sign-in spends one of the 10 recovery codes and no new authenticator can be set up from the page; after the tenth code the admin cannot sign in on the live site (ACC-3).
findings.general_class: Any page flow that keeps working after a call whose answer is a session: Edge.adopt fires edge-auth and the App re-routes under the form (MFA verify then enrol here; also sign-in and register/verify followed by any further step). Also any browser test that stubs an answer in a shape the real route never sends, so the page's real state change is never exercised.
findings.fix: Front-end (static/edge-app.js, static/edge-client.js). Keep the /mfa mode while a set-up resumes: for example authMode returns 'mfa' while authFlow.resumeEnrol is set, or MfaForm calls enroll before adopting the verified session, and goes to the landing page only after the new authenticator is confirmed. Add a signed-in entry 'Set up a new authenticator' (account page 'Password and sign-in') that runs verify, then enrol, then confirm. Replace the stubbed test with one on the real routes (the test_auth_pages_live.py style, site live) that sets up a second authenticator after a recovery code and after the old phone's code.

findings.title: Phone and recovery codes both lost: no way back for the live admin; the operator unlock keeps the enrolment, and nothing removes one
findings.evidence: scripts/edge_mfa_unlock.py:6-7: 'It changes nothing else: the enrolment, the recovery codes, the password and the sessions stay.' It clears only the failure counts and locks (lines 39-52). grep over scripts/ and apps/edge-bff/app/ finds no statement that deletes an mfa_totp row: only FlowStore.enroll replaces an unconfirmed candidate or adds a waiting one. A reset by email clears only counts and locks (auth_flows.py FlowStore.reset, the UPDATE of mfa_totp). The MFA_LOCKED words (errors.py:62) offer waiting 24 hours, a reset by email or the operator unlock; none of them gives a new authenticator. Together with ACC-1, a live admin who loses the phone and runs out of recovery codes can come back only through a hand-written database statement. The beta (switch off, no MFA) keeps working.
findings.general_class: Every account that needs the second factor: user #1 now, Phase 4 admins later. A recovery procedure that names only the counters, never the factor itself.
findings.fix: Operations layer: an audited operator step beside edge_mfa_unlock.py (run_job.sh, private network, an admin_audit row) that removes the account's mfa_totp row and recovery codes and revokes its sessions, so the next sign-in starts the first enrolment. Write it into CONTRACT 4 'Admin MFA' and README. Later, the Phase 4 admin page offers the same for other admins.

findings.title: With the recovery codes locked, the MFA page hides the authenticator-code path and disables Continue, although the authenticator still works
findings.evidence: Local experiment on the live-site build (test_probe_mfa_pages2.py::test_the_lock_of_the_recovery_codes_on_the_page): recovery_failures preset to 9, then two wrong recovery codes. Output: 'message: Too many wrong codes, so this way of signing in is locked. Wait 24 hours or reset your password by email...', 'authenticator toggle shown: 0 Continue enabled: False', 'server: totp locked False recovery locked True'. Screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-saniti/f3bec3b8-f6e3-5a54-b257-4a56b384bdc8/scratchpad/checker_after/exp_recovery_locked.png. Code: static/edge-app.js:864-867 sets locked 'all' whenever details.use is absent and ignores details.locked ('recovery_code', auth_flows.py MFA_LOCKED details); :886-888 hide the toggle while locked and disable Continue when locked === 'all'. The admin, who still has the phone, is told to wait 24 hours; a reload of the page clears it.
findings.general_class: Refusal details that name which way is locked (or limited), read by the page as all-or-nothing: the same reading would hit any future second factor or a per-method limit.
findings.fix: Front-end (static/edge-app.js MfaForm): read details.locked. When it is 'recovery_code', switch back to the authenticator form with Continue enabled and say the recovery codes are locked until unlock_at. Use 'all' only when both are locked (the server can name both). Add a page test with the recovery lock only.

findings.title: Resend's bounce and complaint webhook is not wired: no RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET on edge-bff-live, so every delivery answers 401 and email_suppression is never filled
findings.evidence: `railway variables -s edge-bff-live -e dev --kv | cut -d= -f1` lists no RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and edge-bff has none either. Probe: POST https://app.edgefinance.id/api/v1/hooks/email/resend with no signature gives 401 HOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID. With no secret, mailer.py:229 svix_verify returns False, so any real Resend delivery gets the same 401. The beta's hook answers 404 (switch off), and the EXEC.md Phase 1 step (line 15679) named the beta's URL for the webhook. CONTRACT 5 says 'Bounce or complaint → email_suppression' and section 16 names RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET; the switch-on body planned in .railway/railway.ts:280 lists RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET: preserve(), but the declared live service does not hold it. The site sends real mail now (resend mode), so a bouncing or complaining address keeps getting reset codes.
findings.general_class: An optional secret whose absence fails closed in silence: the start-up logs nothing. It affects every signed provider hook under /api/v1/hooks/ (the Phase 5 payment hook will have the same shape).
findings.fix: Configuration plus start-up check: the user adds a Resend webhook to https://app.edgefinance.id/api/v1/hooks/email/resend (bounced, complained) and enters its whsec_ secret as RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET on edge-bff-live, declared with preserve() in .railway/railway.ts. With the switch on and resend mode, edge-bff logs a start-up line (as with email_sender_off) when no webhook secret is set.

findings.title: Pre-launch: a non-test account's right password counts as a failed sign-in; the 11th try shows the rate limit instead of SIGN_IN_CLOSED, and the count outlives the launch
findings.evidence: Local experiment (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-saniti/f3bec3b8-f6e3-5a54-b257-4a56b384bdc8/scratchpad/checker_after/exp/test_probe_signin_closed.py, pre-launch settings): 11 sign-ins with the right password of a non-test account answered 10 x SIGN_IN_CLOSED, then SIGN_IN_RATE_LIMIT. identities.sign_in_failures read 10 afterwards, and still 10 after the same account signed in with pre-launch turned off. Code: main.py:840 sign_in_try counts the try before the check. The SIGN_IN_CLOSED branch (:875-878) returns before create_session, which clears the count, and before throttle.clear(SIGNIN_LOGIN) (:899). A right password is therefore recorded as a consecutive failure, toward the per-login limit of 10 per 15 minutes and the per-account cap of 100 that still applies after the launch.
findings.general_class: Any refusal decided after the password was proved that returns before the session is made (SIGN_IN_CLOSED now; later gates at sign-in such as a disabled account or payment due) also leaves the failure counters raised.
findings.fix: edge-bff main.py sign-in: in the SIGN_IN_CLOSED branch, call auth.accounts.sign_in_proved(user_id) and throttle.clear(SIGNIN_LOGIN, login_key) before answering 403, as a success does. Add a test that repeats SIGN_IN_CLOSED more than 10 times.

findings.title: The live web process holds the admin's plaintext first password and address (EDGE_ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD, EDGE_ADMIN_EMAIL) although it never reads them
findings.evidence: The two names are in the variable list of edge-bff-live, and the unrendered query shows them as literals, not references. grep finds neither in apps/edge-bff/app/; the only reader is the job's RUN_JOB_EXTRA_VARS (scripts/onboarding/edge_account_login_job.py:7-9, `${{edge-bff-live.EDGE_ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD}}`). The admin's MFA is still not enrolled (smoke: mfa_enrolled false), so until the admin changes the password this variable is the live admin password, inside the environment of the public web process. The lesson of ERRORS M505 is 'a site that does not use a credential does not hold it', which is why config.validate refuses Orc's key on the live site.
findings.general_class: Operator-only values put on a public web service for convenience: the EDGE_ADMIN_* values now, and future test-account or operator values that a job reads by reference.
findings.fix: Railway configuration: keep EDGE_ADMIN_USERNAME, EDGE_ADMIN_EMAIL and EDGE_ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD on a service that serves nothing (the job runner, which edge_account_login_job.py would then reference), or delete EDGE_ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD once the admin has set an own password. Optionally, config.validate on a site refuses EDGE_ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD as it refuses the Orc key. Changing the variables needs the user's approval.

findings.title: Whichever site holds the shared backtest-worker slot takes it again before the other site can: a queue of jobs on one site holds back the other site's jobs, shown as RUNNING the whole time
findings.evidence:
Code:
- backtest.py:574-592: the slot is a pg_try_advisory_lock, with no queue of waiters.
- backtest.py:973-984 (worker_slot): a site that is waiting tries again only after sleep(EDGE_POLL_SECONDS).
- backtest.py:987-1000 and 870-875: the site that holds the slot gives it back at the end of execute(); run() then claims its next job and takes the slot again with no pause, within milliseconds.
- backtest.py:699-710: a job is claimed and marked RUNNING (with started_at and a renewed lease) before it has the slot.

Local probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-saniti/f3bec3b8-f6e3-5a54-b257-4a56b384bdc8/scratchpad/checker_after/test_slot_fairness.py, against the throwaway Postgres, with the OneSlotWorker from test_c3c_site_recheck:
- Setup: two BacktestLoop.run() loops (beta and live), both polling every 0.3 s. Six live jobs from six accounts are queued, and one beta job of user #1 is queued while the first live job runs.
- Result: the jobs reached the worker in the order live x6, then beta: "BETA_POSITION 7 OF 7" in three runs out of three.
- The beta job waited about 5.7 s, the length of all six live jobs, although each live job took about 0.94 s.
- The code is the same on both sides, so the beta's admin (one running and three queued jobs) holds back the live site's users in the same way.
findings.general_class: Any resource the two sites share through a try-lock that one side polls while the holder can take it again at once. Today that is the backtest-worker slot; the housekeeping try-locks are harmless because they only skip a turn. Related: a job counts as RUNNING, and its claim metric (backtest_claim queue_wait_ms) is measured, before the job has the worker, so the page and the timings show a waiting job as running. Pre-launch only the admin and test accounts run backtests; once registration opens, paid accounts on live can hold the admin's beta backtests indefinitely.
findings.fix:
In BacktestStore and BacktestLoop (apps/edge-bff/app/backtest.py), hand the slot over in order across both sites. Two ways:
- Keep a job QUEUED until its loop holds the slot. Whoever holds the slot then picks the oldest waiting job of either site, dispatches its own site's job, or gives the slot back without taking it again when the oldest job is the other site's.
- Or take the slot with a blocking pg_advisory_lock under lock_timeout on a dedicated connection; PostgreSQL grants lock waiters in arrival order.
